discovery: The titanium-doped sapphire laser and Kerr-lens mode-locking, the basis of femtosecond laser science

nominees.name: Wilson Sibbett
nominees.affiliation: University of St Andrews, United Kingdom

motivation: In 1982 Peter Moulton demonstrated the titanium-doped sapphire laser, a gain medium with an extraordinarily broad bandwidth across the near infrared. In 1991 Wilson Sibbett and his St Andrews team found that a Ti:sapphire laser could mode-lock itself through the optical Kerr effect. This simple, robust technique soon produced pulses of only a few femtoseconds. Together these advances replaced fragile dye lasers with turnkey femtosecond sources. Nearly every ultrafast laboratory in the world now runs on Ti:sapphire oscillators and amplifiers. They power femtochemistry, attosecond pulse generation, optical frequency combs, multiphoton microscopy, high-field physics and chirped-pulse-amplified petawatt systems. Several Nobel Prizes have depended on this enabling platform, but its inventors have never been recognised. Their work is a model of how a clever experimental idea can remove a technical barrier and open whole fields of physics, chemistry and medicine.
